lib/git.js.Pattern: Command string construction from user inputs passed into Git CLI wrapper functions
lib/git.js.Static Analysis Risk: Command Injection via dynamic command construction
lib/git.js.Failure: User-controlled parameters are concatenated into shell commands that are later executed via spawn/exec. Static analysis struggles to track sanitization across multiple wrapper functions and method calls, especially when arguments are conditionally appended.

lib/runners/promise-wrapped.js.Pattern: Asynchronous wrapping of command execution using Promises
lib/runners/promise-wrapped.js.Failure: Execution flow is deferred through Promises, making it difficult for static analysis to connect input sources to eventual command execution sinks. This breaks straightforward control-flow reasoning and requires interprocedural async modeling.

lib/utils.js.Pattern: String concatenation and transformation of command arguments
lib/utils.js.Failure: Command arguments are constructed indirectly through helper functions, making it difficult for static analysis to trace tainted input propagation across utility layers.
